c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, meaning its due, its obligatory zakat, on the day it is measured or its measure is known.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest

, that is, when a man planted, it was his day of harvest, which is that he would know what his measure and his due were, so he would take out one from every ten, and what the people would pick up from its ears.

c: Bishr told us, Yazid told us, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest

, and its due on the day of its harvest, is the obligatory charity. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, established the law of giving a full tenth of what was watered by the sky or a flowing spring, or was watered by dew - and dew is the first - or was rain-fed. And if it was watered by a bribe, half of the tenth. Qatada said: This is regarding the fruit that is measured. And this was when the fruit reached five wasqs, which is one-third of a hundred sa’s, then zakat was due on it. And they preferred to give an amount equal to that of the fruit that was not measured.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada and Tawus:
m: h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, they said: It is zakat.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Salim Al-Makki, on the authority of Muhammad bin Al-Hanafiyyah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, he said: on the day of its measurement, he gives a tenth or half a tenth.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Salim Al-Makki, on the authority of Muhammad Ibn Al-Hanafiyyah,
m: his saying:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, he said: A tenth and half a tenth.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, and on the authority of Qatada:
m: h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, they said: Zakat.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Ishaq told us, he said, Abu Muawiyah Al-Dharee’ told us, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, he said: a tenth and half a tenth.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Al-Hakam bin Utaybah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: the same.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, meaning: on the day of its measurement, whether it was wheat, dates, or raisins. And its due is its zakat.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement:
h
Eat of its fruit when it bears fruit and give its due on the day of its harvest
, he said: Eat from it, and when you harvest it, give its due, and its due is its tenth.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Yunus Ibn ʿUbayd, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: He said regarding this verse:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, he said: The zakat is when you harvest it.

c: Amr told us, he said, Muhammad bin Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Rajaʿ, he said:
m: I asked Al-Hasan about his statement:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, he said: Zakat.

c: Ibn Al-Barqi told me, he said, Amr bin Abi Salamah told us, he said:
m: I asked Ibn Zayd bin Aslam about the statement of God:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, so I said to him: Is it the tithe? He said: Yes! So I said to him: On the authority of your father? He said: On the authority of my father and others.

x: Others said: Rather, it is a right that God has made obligatory in the money of those who have money, other than the obligatory charity.
Who said that?

c: Amr bin Ali told us, he said, Abdul Wahhab told us, he said, Muhammad bin Jaafar told us, on the authority of his father:
m: h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, he said: Something other than the due due, he said: And it was in his book: On the authority of Ali bin Al-Hussein.

c: Amr told us, Yahya told us, Abdul Malik told us, on the authority of Ata’,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, he said: A handful of food.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Bakr told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’:
m: h
And give its due on the day of its harvest

, for wealth: from palm trees, grapes, and all grain. Ibn Wakee’ narrated, he said: Muhammad ibn Bakr narrated, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: I said to Ata’: What do you think of the fruits you harvest? He said: And some of them are also given. And he said: From everything you harvest, you give its due on the day of its harvest, from palm trees, grapes, grains, fruits, greens, or sugar cane, from everything of that. I said to Ata’: Is all of that obligatory upon the people? He said: Yes! Then he recited:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
. He said: I said to Ata’:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest

. Is there something specific and specific about that? He said: No. Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Abd al-Malik, on the authority of Ata’, regarding his statement:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, he said: He gives from those present on that day what is easy, and it is not zakat.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Isa bin Yunus told us, on the authority of Abdul Malik, on the authority of Ata’:
m: h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, he said: It is not zakat, but whoever is present at that time should feed his harvest.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-Ala’ bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of Hammad:
m: h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, he said: They were given fresh dates.

c: Ibn Humayd and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And give its due on the day of its harvest

, he said: When the poor are present, throw some of it away for them. And when you have cleaned it and taken its measure, gather some of it for them. And when you know its measure, set aside its zakat. And when you have taken the harvest of the date palms, throw some of the dates away for them. And when you have taken its measure, gather some of it for them. And when you know its measure, set aside its zakat.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, he said: other than the obligatory portion. Ibn Humayd narrated, he said, Hakam narrated, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest

. He said: It is thrown to the questioners at the time of harvest from the ears of corn, and if it is mud - or clay, Abu Jaʿfar is not sure - it is thrown to them. Then if he carries it and wants to make it into a pile, he throws it to them. And if it is trampled, he feeds them from it. And if he is finished and knows how much he has measured, he sets aside its zakat. And he said about palm trees: When harvesting, he feeds them from the fruit and the spikes. And if it is at its measurement, he feeds them from the dates. And if he is finished, he sets aside its zakat.

c: Amr bin Ali and Muhammad bin Bashar told us, they said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, he said: When the crop is harvested, it throws off the ears of corn, and when the palm trees are ripe, it throws off the clusters of dates. So when it is measured, it pays zakat on it.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: At the time of harvest, at the time of threshing, and at the time of harvesting, he takes from it for them, and when he measures it, he sets aside its zakat. And on his authority, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mujahid, the same, except that he said: other than zakat.

c: Amr bin Ali told us, Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, he said: Something other than zakat, in the harvest and the harvesting, when they harvest and when they measure.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Isa, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh,
m: regarding the statement of God:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, he said: It is obligatory, when it is harvested.

c: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad Ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: that he said
m: regarding this verse:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, he said: When it is harvested, it is fed, and when it is put into the threshing floor, and when it is trampled, it is fed from it.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ibn Umar, he said:
m: The poor person is to be fed, other than what he is given of the tithe and half of the tithe. Surat al-An’am 6:141
h
And it is He who produced gardens trellised
and untrellised, and palm trees and crops of varying fruit, and olives and pomegranates, some similar and some dissimilar.
h
Eat of its fruit when it bears fruit
h
and give its due on the day of its harvest
h
and do not be excessive

. Indeed, He does not like the extravagant. And on his authority, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: A handful at harvest time, and a handful at the time of harvest.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hafs told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, he said:
m: They used to give something to those who came to them.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: The bundle Ibn Bashar told us, Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said:
m: He gives something like a bunch of dates.

c: Amr bin Ali told us, Yahya bin Saeed told us, Sufyan told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, he said: Something like this from the bunch, and Yahya placed his thumb on the second joint of the index finger.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: It is similar to a bundle.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abu Jaafar, and on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Hammad, on the authority of Ibrahim, they said:
m: He gives a bundle. Amr ibn Ali narrated, Kathir ibn Hisham narrated, Jaafar ibn Burqan narrated, on the authority of Yazid ibn al-Asamm, who said: When the palm trees were harvested, a man would bring a bunch of dates from his palm tree and hang it on the side of the mosque. A poor person would come and hit it with his stick, and when it fell apart, he would eat from it. Then the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) entered with Hasan or Husayn, and he took a date and pulled it out of his mouth. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not eat charity, nor did his family. That is why God said:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Khalid bin Hayyan told us, on the authority of Ja’far bin Burqan, on the authority of Maimun bin Mihran and Yazid bin Al-A’sam, they said:
m: When the people of Medina harvested, they would bring the bunch of dates and put them in the mosque, then the beggar would come and hit it with his stick and it would fall from it, and this is what He said:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
b.via: Maimun bin Mihran and Yazid bin Al-A’sam

c: Ali bin Sahl told us, Zaid bin Abi Al-Zarqa told us, on the authority of Jaʿfar, on the authority of Yazid and Maymun,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest

, they said: When a man harvested the date palms, he would bring the clusters and hang them on the side of the mosque, and a knife would come to him and strike it with his stick, and he would eat what fell from it.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ubaidullah told us, on the authority of Abu Jaafar Al-Razi, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas:
m: h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, he said: the ears of corn were picked.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Abdul Karim Al-Jazari, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: They used to hang the cluster of dates in the mosque near the fire, and the weak would eat from it. And with it, on the authority of Muammar, he said, Mujahid said:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, meaning that something is fed when it is harvested.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hammani told us, he said, Sharik told us, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, he said: the bunch, and what falls from the ear of corn. And on his authority, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, he said: fodder.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, he said: This was before zakat, for the poor, a handful and a bunch of it for fodder for his beast.

c: Amr bin Ali told us, Abu Asim told us, Muhammad bin Rafa’ah told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, he said: Whether it is little or much.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said, Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh:
m: h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, he said: When planting, he gives what is due, and when harvesting, he gives what is due, and by leaving them, they follow the traces of harvesting.

x: Others said: This was something that God commanded the believers to do before the temporary charity was imposed on them. Then the known charity abrogated it. So there is no obligation on wealth, whatever it may be, whether it is a crop or a plant, except the charity that God imposed on it.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Muqsim, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: It was abrogated by ten and half a tenth.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Hafs told us, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said:
m: It was abrogated by ten and half a tenth. And on his authority, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Ibn al-Hanafiyyah, he said: It was abrogated by ten and half a tenth.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Salim, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
. He said: This was before zakat, then when zakat was revealed it abrogated it, so they would give the bunch of dates.

c: Ibn Hamid and Ibn Wakee’ told us, they said: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Shabak, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
. He said: They used to do that until the age of ten and a half ten. Then when the age of ten and a half ten was reached, he stopped.

c: Amr bin Ali told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Shabak, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, he said: It is abrogated, its abrogation is the tenth and half of the tenth.

c: Ibn Bashar told us, he said, Yahya told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim:
m: h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, he said: It was abrogated by a tenth and half a tenth.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Shabak, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said:
m: Its copy is ten and half a tenth. And on his authority, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: Zakat abrogated it. And on his authority, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of al-Suddi, he said: It was abrogated by zakat:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest

c: Yaqub told me, he said, Hisham told us, he said, Mughira told us, on the authority of Shabak, on the authority of Ibrahim,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest

, he said: This surah is Meccan, and it was abrogated by a tenth and a half of a tenth. I said: From whom? He said: From the scholars. And on his authority, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Shabak, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: Its abrogation is ten and half a tenth.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: As for
h
and give its due on the day of its harvest

, it was when someone passed by them on the day of harvest or the harvesting, they would feed him from it, so God abrogated it for them with zakat, and it was for what the earth produced, a tenth and half a tenth.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abd Al-A’la told us, on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said:
m: They used to submit to their kinship with the polytheists.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Atiyah:
m: h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, he said: It was abrogated by the tenth and half of the tenth. They used to give when they harvested and when they winnowed, then it was abrogated by the tenth and half a tenth.

x: The most correct of the sayings in this regard, in my opinion, is the saying of those who said: It was an obligation imposed by God on the believers in their food and fruits that their crops and plants produce, then God abrogated it with the obligatory charity and the known duty of the tenth and half a tenth. This is because everyone is unanimously agreed, with no disagreement among them: that the charity on tillage is not taken except after threshing, cleaning and winnowing, and that the charity on dates is not taken except after the harvest. If that is the case, and His Most High’s saying:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest

, indicates that it is an order from God Most High to give its due on the day of its harvest, and the day of its harvest is the day of its harvest and its cutting, and the grain is undoubtedly in its ear on that day, and the dates, even if they are the fruit of a palm tree or a grapevine, are not completely dry and withered, and the charity from the grain is only taken after it has been threshed, winnowed, and purified by measuring, and the charity from the dates is only taken after they have completely dried and withered by measuring, then it is known that what is taken as charity after the time of its harvest is not what must be given to the poor on the day of its harvest.
Why do you deny that this is an obligation from God regarding money, other than the obligatory charity?

Because it is either an obligatory duty or a voluntary act. If it is an obligatory duty, then it must be the way of the obligatory charity, and whoever neglects to pay it to its people is sinful towards his Lord and disobeys His command. And in establishing the argument that there is no obligation on wealth after zakat that makes the obligation of zakat compulsory other than what is obligatory for the expenses of those for whom a person is obligated to spend, what indicates that this is not the case. Or it could be a voluntary act. If that is the case, then the choice must be made in giving it to the owner of the crops and fruits.

And in the statement of those who say that this is obligatory, there is what indicates that this is not the case. If the verse is not intended to be a recommendation, and it is not permissible for it to have an outlet for the obligation of it at this time, then it is known that it has been abrogated. What supports what we have said about this statement as evidence of its correctness is that He, the Most High, followed His statement,
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, with, “And be not excessive. Indeed, He does not like those who commit excess.” It is known that one of the rulings of God regarding His Surat al-An’am 6:141
h
And it is He who produced gardens trellised
and untrellised, and palm trees and crops of varying fruit, and olives and pomegranates, some similar and some dissimilar.
h
Eat of its fruit when it bears fruit
h
and give its due on the day of its harvest
h
and do not be excessive

Indeed, He does not like the extravagant. servants since He imposed the obligatory, temporary charity on their wealth is that the one who takes it is their leaders and shepherds. If that is the case, then what is the reason for the owner of the wealth to be forbidden from being excessive in giving it, when the one who takes it is compelled, and he only takes the right that God imposed on it. If someone thinks that this is only a prohibition from God, the Guardian, to take that from the shepherds, from transgressing against the owner of the money, and going beyond taking what he is not permitted to take, then the last part of the verse, which is His saying: And be not extravagant, is connected to the first part, which is His saying:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest

. So if the one who is forbidden from extravagance is the one who collects that, then it may be necessary that the one who is commanded to give it is the one who is forbidden from being extravagant in it, and that is the ruler.

This is a statement that, if someone were to say it, would be outside the scope of all the people of interpretation, and would contradict the usual discourse. This is sufficient evidence of his error.
What is wrong with the meaning of his statement:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest

, and give its due on the day of its measurement, not on the day of its cutting and severing, nor on the day of its harvesting and reaping? You know who among the people of interpretation said that. That is what: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told us, Hisham told us, Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, regarding his statement:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest

, he said: the day of its measurement. Al-Muthanna told us, he said, Amr bin Awn told us, he said, Hisham told us, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Salim Al-Makki, on the authority of Muhammad bin Al-Hanafiyyah, regarding his statement:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, he said: on the day of its measurement, he gives a tenth and half a tenth. With others who have mentioned the narration previously about them?

Because the day of its measurement is not the day of its harvest. The meaning of those who say this statement will not be without one of two things: Either they directed the meaning of harvest to the meaning of measuring, and that is not reasonable in the speech of the Arabs, because harvest and harvesting in their speech: the grandfather and the cutting, not the measuring, or they directed the interpretation of his saying:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest to

: And give its due after the day of its harvest if you measure it, and that is contrary to the apparent meaning of the revelation. That is because the command in the apparent revelation is to give its due on the day of its harvest, not after the day of its harvest. There is no difference between one who says: - God only meant by his saying:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest

, after the day of its harvest, and another who said: He meant by that before the day of its harvest, because they are both saying a statement, the evidence of the apparent revelation is contrary to it.
The people of interpretation differed about the extravagance that God forbade in this verse, and who is forbidden.

Some of them said: What is prohibited is the owner of the palm trees, crops and fruits, and the extravagance that God prohibited in this verse is exceeding the amount in giving to what would be unfair to the owner of the money.
Who said that?

c: Amr bin Ali told us, Al-Mu'tamir bin Sulaiman told us, Asim told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest

, and be not excessive, the verse, he said: They used to give something other than zakat, then they were excessive, so God revealed: “And be not excessive. Indeed, He does not like those who commit excess.”

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Asim Al-Ahwal, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah:
m: h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, he said: They used to give something on the day of the harvest other than the zakat, then they competed over it and were extravagant, so God said: “
h
And do not be extravagant
. Indeed, He does not like the extravagant.”

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Asim Al-Ahwal, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah:
m: h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
, he said: They used to give something on the day of the harvest, then they were extravagant, so God said: “
h
And do not be extravagant
. Indeed, He does not like the extravagant.”

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said:
m: It was revealed about Thabit bin Qais bin Shammas, who cut down a palm tree and said: Let no one come today without me feeding him! So he fed him, until evening came and he had no fruit. Then God said: “And be not excessive. Indeed, He does not like those who commit excess.” Ibn Wakee’ narrated, he said: Muhammad ibn Bakr narrated, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: I said to Ata’:
h
And do not be extravagant

, does he say: Do not be extravagant in what is brought on the day of harvest, or in everything? He said: Yes! In everything, it forbids extravagance. He said: Then I returned to him after a while and said: What does His statement:
h
And do not be extravagant
, for He does not like those who commit excess mean? He said: It forbids extravagance in everything, then he recited: They neither were extravagant nor niggardly.

c: Amr bin Ali told us, Yazid bin Harun told us, Sufyan bin Hussein told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, who said:
m: People went around Iyas bin Muawiyah in Kufa and asked him: What is extravagance? He said: Whatever is less than the command of God is extravagance.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And do not be extravagant
, do not give your money away and become poor.

x: Others said: The extravagance that God forbade in this place is withholding charity and the right that God commanded the owner of the wealth to give to its people by His saying:
h
And give its due on the day of its harvest
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Bakr told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said, Abu Bakr ibn Abdullah told me, on the authority of Amr ibn Salim and others, on the authority of Saeed ibn al-Musayyab,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not be extravagant
, he said: Do not withhold charity, lest you disobey.

c: Amr bin Ali told us, he said, Muhammad bin Al-Zubayrkan told us, he said, Musa bin Ubaidah told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b:
m: h
And do not be extravagant
. Indeed, He does not like those who commit excess.” Extravagance means not giving what is right.

x: Others said: The Sultan was addressed with this. He was forbidden to take from the owner of the money more than what he was obligated to give him.
Who said that?

c: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
And do not be extravagant
, he said: He said to the ruler: Do not be extravagant, do not take unjustly, so this verse was between the ruler and the people, meaning his statement:
h
Eat of its fruit when it bears fruit
, the verse.

x: The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that God Almighty forbade, with His saying:
h
And do not be excessive

, all meanings of extravagance, and He did not specify one meaning over another. Since this is the case, and extravagance in the speech of the Arabs is: error in hitting the right in the gift, either by exceeding its limit in excess, or by falling short of its required limit, it was known that the one who distributes his money is a competition, and the one who spends it among people until his gift is unfair to him, is extravagant in exceeding the limit of God to what is not his. Likewise the one who falls short in spending in what God has obligated him to spend in, and that is like his preventing what he is obligated to give from it to the people of the two shares of charity when it is obligatory for it, or preventing the one who is obligated to spend from his family and children what he is obligated to from it.

Likewise the ruler in taking from his subjects what God has not permitted him to take. All of these in what they did of that are extravagant, and are included in the meaning of the one who did what God forbade of extravagance in His saying:
h
And do not be extravagant

in giving from your money what is unfair to you, since what preceded it from the speech was a command from God to give what is due to its people on the day of harvest. The verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for a specific reason, and the ruling on it is general, and indeed, the general verses of the Qur’an are like that. So is His statement: “
h
And do not be excessive
. Indeed, He does not like those who commit excess.”

i: And the evidence for the correctness of what we said about the meaning of extravagance is that, as we said, the poet said:
x: They gave Hanida eight hundred dirhams, and there was no extravagance in their giving.
It means extravagance: error in giving.

God Almighty says: And He created from the livestock loads and furnishings, in addition to what He created from the gardens, trellised and untrellised. The load, what is carried on it of camels and other things. And the camels that are not yet mature enough to be carried.
The interpreters differed in their interpretation of this.
Some of them said: The load is what is carried on the large and old camels, and the litter is the young ones that are not carried on because of their smallness.
Who said that?

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: regarding his statement: Hawl and Furshan, he said: Hawl is the large camels, and Furshan is the small camels. He said, my father told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr al-Hudhali, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Humulah refers to the large, small, and furry camels.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ubaid God told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Yahya, on the authority of Mujahid, who said:
m: The load is what is carried from the camels, and the bedding is what is not carried. And on his authority, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Mujahid: The load is what is carried from the camels, and the bedding is what is not carried.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: And small camels, he said: small camels.

c: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said, Abd al-Rahman told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah,
m: regarding his statement:
h
A load and a bed
, he said: The load! are the adults, and the bed are the children.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, on the authority of Ibn Masoud,
m: regarding his statement:
h
A load and a bed
, the load is what the camels carry, and the bed is the small ones.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, he said, Shuʿbah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu al-Ahwas, on the authority of Abdullah: that he said
m: regarding this verse:
h
A load and a bed
, he said: The load is what is carried on it of camels, and the bed is the small ones. Ibn al-Muthanna said, Muhammad said, Shuʿbah said:
It was only Sufyan who told me, on the authority of Abu Ishaq.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Al-Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, he said, Al-Hasan said:
m: The load, from camels and cows.

x: Some of them said: The load is from the camels, and what is not from the load is the bed.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of al-Hasan,
m: h
A load and a mattress
. He said: The load is what it is carried on, and the mattresses are its edges, meaning its small ones.

c: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
And among the livestock are loads and saddles

. So the load is what the camels carry, and the saddles are the young camels, the young camels and what is less than that which is not carried. It is said: the load, of cows and camels, and the brush, of sheep.

x: Others said: The load is what is carried on it of camels, horses, mules, etc., and the fursh is the sheep.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And among the livestock are loads and beds
. As for the loads, they are camels, horses, mules, donkeys, and everything that is carried on. As for the beds, they are sheep.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ubaidullah told us, on the authority of Abu Jaafar, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas:
m: The load, from camels and cows, and fursha are goats and sheep. Surat al-An’am 6:142 And among the grazing livestock are burdens and furnishings. Eat of what God has provided for you
h
and do not follow the footsteps of Satan
. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And among the livestock are burdens and furnishings
, he said: As for the burden, they are camels and cows. He said: As for the furnishings, they are sheep.

c: Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said, Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Other than Al-Hasan, he used to say: The load is camels and cows, and the fursh is sheep.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: h
And among the livestock are loads and beds
. As for the load, it is the camels, and as for the beds, it is the two young camels, the young sheep, and the sheep. And whatever is carried on it is a load.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement:
h
A load and a bed
, the load is the camels, and the bed is the sheep.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, my father told us, on the authority of Abu Bakr Al-Hudhali, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: And furshan, he said: The furs are the sheep.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
A load and a mattress
, he said: The load is what you ride, and the mattress is what you eat and milk, a sheep that does not carry a load, you eat its meat, and you make a blanket and a mattress from its wool.

x: The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that the humulah refers to what is carried from the livestock, because that is a characteristic of them when they carry, not that it is a name for them, like camels, horses, and mules. If it is only called humulah because it carries, then it is obligatory for everything that is carried on the back of the livestock to be humulah. It is a plural that does not have a singular from its word, like rakubah and jazura. Likewise, fursh is only a description of what is soft and close to the ground in its body, and it is called fursh. I think it was called that to represent it in the straightness of its teeth and its softness with the fursh of the ground, which is the flat ground on which people perform ablution. As for the word hamulah, with the letter ha pronounced with a damma, it refers to the loads, and it is also hamul with the letter ha pronounced with a damma.

God Almighty says: Eat of what God has provided for you, O believers. He has made lawful for you the fruits of your crops and your plants, and the meat of your livestock, since the polytheists forbade some of that for themselves, so they made a share for God from what He created of crops and livestock and a share for Satan, so they said: This is for God, according to their claim, and this is for our partners, “
h
And do not follow the footsteps of Satan

,” as the sailors of the lake and those who let loose the free-range animals followed, so you forbid yourselves from the good provision of God that He provided for you what they forbade, so you obey Satan and disobey the Most Merciful with it, as:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement,
h
And do not follow the footsteps of Satan

, do not follow his obedience, it is sins for you, and it is obedience to the wicked. Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you who seeks your destruction and to turn you away from the path of your Lord, clear, he has made his enmity clear to you, by his opposition to your father in enmity, until he expelled him from Paradise with his plot and deception, out of envy of him and malice towards him.

x: This is a rebuke from God, the Most High, to the idolaters who are just with Him, who sailed the seas, set the free animals free, and connected the connections, and a teaching from Him to His Prophet Jumzat and the believers in him, the proof against them in their prohibition of what they prohibited from that. So He said to the believers in Him and His Messenger: And it is He who created gardens, trellised and untrellised, and from the bounty He created burdens and furnishings. Then He, the Most High, explained the burdens and furnishings, and said: eight pairs. The word eight is in the accusative case because it is a translation of load and furnishings, and a substitute for them. It is as if the meaning of the statement is: And from the livestock He created eight pairs. So when He presented load and furnishings before the eight, He explained that later and said: eight pairs, according to that meaning.

Of the sheep two and of the goats two, that is four, because each of the two sheep is a pair, so the female is the pair of the male, and the male is the pair of the female, and likewise of the goats and of all the other animals.

Therefore, the Most High said: Eight pairs, as He said: And of everything We have created mates, because the male is the pair of the female, and the female is the pair of the male, so even if they are two, they are two pairs, as the Most High said: And He made from her her mate that he might dwell in tranquility with her, and as He said: Keep your wife for yourself, and as:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak:
m: Of the sheep two, a male and a female, Of the cows two, a male and a female, Of the camels two, a male and a female. And two are called a pair, as Labid said: From every guarded one, his stick remains, his wife is upon him, his word and his punishment Then he said to them: Eat from what God has provided you of these fruits and meats, and ride this load, O believers, and do not follow the footsteps of Satan in forbidding what these ignorant people have forbidden without my ordering them to do so. Say, O Muhammad, to those who have forbidden what they have forbidden of tillage and livestock, following Satan, from the worshippers of idols and statues who claimed that God has forbidden them what they have forbidden of that: Is it the two males that your Lord has forbidden, O liars against God, of sheep and goats? For if they claim that and acknowledge it, they have lied to themselves and revealed their ignorance. For if they say: The two males are forbidden of that, they have made it obligatory to prohibit every two males from the offspring of sheep and goats, and they enjoy the meat of the two males among them and their backs. In that is the corruption of their claim and the falsity of their saying, Or the two females, for if they say: Our Lord has forbidden the two females, they have made it obligatory to prohibit the meat of every female from the offspring of sheep and goats for themselves and their backs. This also belies them and refutes their claim that their Lord forbade them that, since they were enjoying the meat of some of that and its backs, or what the wombs of the two females contain, meaning the wombs of female sheep and female goats. That is why He said, the wombs of the two females. This also belies that if they had acknowledged it and said, It is forbidden to us, or what the wombs of the two females contain, their statement would be long and their lie would be clear, because they were acknowledging that God forbade them male sheep and goats and their females, that they should eat their meat or ride their backs, and they were enjoying some of their males with their females. And what is in His statement:
h
And what the wombs of the two females contain

, is the accusative in apposition to the two females. “Inform me with knowledge,” meaning: Say to them: Inform me with knowledge of that, as to its authenticity: which of that has your Lord forbidden you, and how He forbade it? If you are truthful, in what you attribute to your Lord of your claim, and what you attribute to Him of your prohibition. Rather, this is an announcement from God, may He be glorified, to His Prophet that everything these polytheists said about this and attributed to God is a lie against God, and that He did not forbid anything of this, and that they only followed in the footsteps of Satan and disobeyed his command. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said in interpreting that.

x: Who said that?

c: Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Eight pairs of sheep
, two and of goats, two the verse, that I did not forbid any of this, little or much, male or female.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Two of the sheep and two of the goats. He said: Ask them: Has He forbidden the two males, or the two females, or what the wombs of the two females contain? That is: I have not forbidden anything of this, with knowledge, if you should be truthful. So he mentioned something similar to that from camels and cows.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: eight pairs, regarding what God forbade of the bahīrah.

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Husayn told us, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement: eight pairs, he said: This is regarding what God has forbidden of lakes and swine. Ibn Jurayj said: He says: Where did you forbid this? From the males or from the females? Did the wombs of the females not contain it? Because they only contain a male or a female, so where did the prohibition come from? They answered: We found our fathers doing that.

c: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi:
m: h
Eight pairs of sheep

, two of goats, two of cows, and two of camels. He says: I have sent down to you eight pairs of what I have counted, male and female. So the two males have been forbidden to you, or the two females? Have the wombs of the two females not included it? He says: That is, what the wombs of the two females contain, they only include a male or a female. So neither male nor female of the eight have been forbidden to you. This was only mentioned because of what they were forbidden of the livestock.

c: Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me, he said, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan:
m: h
And what the wombs of the two females contain
, he said: What the womb carries.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: about His statement, Say, ‘Is it the two males that are forbidden or the two females?’ He said, this is because of their statement, What is in the bellies of these livestock is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our wives. He said, and Ibn Zayd said about His statement,
h
Eight pairs of sheep
, two, and of goats, two, He said: The livestock are the camels, cows, sheep, and goats, these livestock about which God said, Eight pairs. He said, and he said about His statement,
h
These are livestock and tillage which are forbidden
, We keep them restricted for whomever we want, and from whomever we want. And His statement,
h
And livestock whose backs are forbidden

, He said, no one rides them, And livestock over which they do not mention the name of God, He said, Is it the two males that are forbidden or the two females? Which of these two is forbidden to these? That is, that they are permissible for these, and forbidden to those. - Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying: “Eight pairs: of sheep, two, and of goats, two. Say: Is it the two males He has forbidden, or the two females, or what the wombs of the two females contain?” He means: Does the womb contain anything but a male or a female? So do they forbid some and permit others?

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas,
m: regarding his statement:
h
Eight pairs of sheep

, two of them, and of goats, two of them, so these are four pairs, “And of camels, two of them, and of cattle, two of them. Say, “Has He forbidden the two males or the two females?” He said: I did not forbid any of that. Inform me with knowledge, if you should be truthful, he said: All of it is permissible. Sheep is a plural noun that has no singular form. Sheep can be pluralized as day’in and day’in, like barley and barley, just as slave is pluralized as ‘ubeed and ‘ubeed. As for the singular of the males, it is da’in lama, and the female is da’inah, and the plural of da’inah is da’in. Likewise, goats are pluralized as more than one, as is the goat. As for goats, its plural is mawa’iz.

x: The interpretation of His statement: "
h
And of camels

, two, and of cattle, two. Say: Has He forbidden the two males, or the two females, or what the wombs of the two females contain?" is similar to the interpretation of His statement: Of sheep, two, and of goats, two. These are four pairs, in the same way as we explained about the four pairs before of sheep and goats, so that is eight pairs, as God, the Most High, described. As for His statement:
h
Or were you witnesses when God enjoined this upon you

? Who is more unjust than he who invents a lie against God to lead people astray without knowledge? God, the Most High, commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to say to these ignorant polytheists whose stories he related in these verses that have passed. He, the Most High, says to him: Say to them, O Muhammad: Which of these I asked you about prohibiting has your Lord forbidden you from these eight pairs?

If they answer you about something you asked them about, then say to them: Did you say that God has forbidden this to you, and a messenger from your Lord informed you about it? Or did you witness your Lord and see Him and He commanded you to do what you say and fabricate about God? For what you say of your reports from God that it is forbidden according to what you claim, according to what you claim, is not known except by revelation from Him with a messenger He sends to His creation, or by hearing from Him. So by which of these two aspects did you know that God has forbidden this in this way, through a messenger He sent to you? So inform me with knowledge if you are truthful. Or did you witness your Lord and He commanded you to do this and said to you: I have forbidden this to you, and you heard His prohibition from Him and His covenant with you about it? For neither of these two matters happened.

God the Almighty says: Who is more unjust than he who invents a lie against God? He says: Who is more unjust to himself, and further from the truth than he who invents a lie against God, and adds to it the prohibition of what He has not prohibited, and the permissibility of what He has not permitted, to mislead people without knowledge, He says: To turn them away from His path, Indeed, God does not guide the wrongdoing people, He says: God does not guide to the right path whoever invents a lie against God and speaks falsehood and lies about Him, and adds to it the prohibition of what He has not prohibited, out of disbelief in God and denial of the prophethood of His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, like the one who:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
Or were you witnesses when God enjoined upon you this
, what you say.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, he said:
m: They used to say, meaning those who used to make lakes and swā’ib: God has commanded this. So God said: Who is more unjust than he who invents a lie against God to lead people astray without knowledge?

x: The Most High says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to those who have assigned to God a share of what He has created of crops and livestock, and to their partners among the gods and equals the same, and those who say: These are livestock and crops of a place that no one can eat except whom We will, according to their claim, and those who forbid some of the livestock whose appearance has been delayed, and those who abandon the mention of the name of God over the last of them, and those who forbid some of what is in the bellies of some of their livestock to their females and their wives, and permit it to their males, those who forbid what God has provided for them, fabricating against God, and attributing what they forbid of that to the fact that God is the One who forbade it to them: Has a Messenger from God come to you forbidding that to you, so inform us about it, or has God commanded you to forbid it by witnessing it from you, so you heard from him forbidding that to you and so you forbade it? For you are liars if you claim that, and you cannot claim it, because if you claim it, people will know that you are lying.

I do not find in what was revealed to me of His Book and the verses of His revelation anything forbidden to an eater who eats what you mention that He has forbidden from these livestock that you describe as forbidden what He has forbidden to you from them, according to your claim, unless it be a dead animal, that is, it died without being slaughtered, or blood poured forth, which is the place of slaughter, or unless it be the flesh of a pig, for it is impure or an act of immorality, He says: or unless it be an act of immorality, meaning, by that: or unless it be slaughtered, slaughtered by a polytheist who worships idols for his idol and his gods, and he mentioned the name of his idol over it, for that slaughter is an act of immorality that God has forbidden and made unlawful, and He has forbidden whoever believes in Him from eating what was slaughtered in that way, because it is a dead animal.

This is an announcement from God, may He be glorified, to the polytheists who argued with the Prophet of God and his companions about the prohibition of dead meat, that what they argued with them about is the forbidden thing that God has prohibited, and that what they claimed that God has prohibited is permissible, God has permitted it, and that they lied about their attribution of its prohibition to God. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father,
m: regarding his statement: Say, ‘I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden,’ he said: The people of the Age of Ignorance used to forbid some things and permit others, so he said: Say, ‘I do not find of what you used to forbid and permit except this: Except it be a dead animal or blood poured forth or the flesh of swine, for indeed it is impure, or an abomination dedicated to other than God.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father,
m: regarding His statement: Say, ‘I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden,’ the verse, he said: The people of ignorance considered some things permissible and others forbidden, so God said to His Prophet: Say, ‘I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden from what you used to consider permissible except this.’ There were some things that they used to consider forbidden, but they are forbidden now.

c: Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said, Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said, Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father:
m: Say, ‘I do not find within what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to one who would eat it,’ he said: What is eaten. I said: In the Age of Ignorance? He said: “Yes, and that is what he used to say: ‘Except it be a dead animal or blood poured forth.’” Ibn Jurayj said: Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr informed me, on the authority of Mujahid: Say, ‘I do not find within what has been revealed to me anything forbidden,’ he said: From what they used to eat in the Age of Ignorance, I do not find anything forbidden to one who would eat it, except it be a dead animal or blood poured forth. As for his saying: or spilled blood, its meaning is: or flowing, shed blood. It is said: I spilled his blood, if I made it flow, I made it flow, so it is spilled blood, as Tarafa bin al-Abd said: I found you, I did not satirize you, nor did I erect idols over which blood is shed. As Ubaid bin Al-Abrash said: If women return to it, they shed tears after the ringing Meaning: They poured and shed tears. And in His stipulation, may He be glorified, regarding blood when He informs His servants of His prohibition of it, that which is spilled and not otherwise, there is clear evidence that whatever is not spilled is permissible and not impure. This is like that which:

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: Or spilled blood, he said: If it were not for this verse, the Muslims would have pursued the veins as the Jews pursued.

c: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: something similar, except that he said: The Muslims would not follow.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Ibn Uyaynah, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ikrimah,
m: something similar.

c: Abu Kuraib told us, he said, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Imran bin Hudayr, on the authority of Abu Majlaz,
m: in the pot, the redness of blood rising from it. He said: God only forbade spilled blood.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Imran bin Hudayr, on the authority of Abu Majlaz, he said:
m: I asked him about blood and what gets stained on the slaughterhouse from the head, and about the pot in which redness is seen? He said: God only forbade spilled blood.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Or spilled blood, he said: What is forbidden is blood that has been spilled. As for meat mixed with blood, there is nothing wrong with it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying: Say, I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to one who would eat it, unless it be dead meat or blood poured forth, meaning: spilled.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, Ibn Dinar told me, on the authority of Ikrimah:
m: Or blood poured out, he said: If it were not for this verse, the Muslims would have followed the veins of the flesh as the Jews did.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Muhammad, on the authority of Aisha:
m: that she did not see anything wrong with the meat of wild animals, and the redness and blood are wrong according to the quantity, and she recited this verse: Say, I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to one who would eat it.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Suwaid told us, he said, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Saeed, he said, Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad told me, on the authority of Aisha, she said,
m: and she mentioned this verse: Or blood poured forth, I said: And the pot can be seen to contain the yellowness in its water. We have explained the meaning of filth in the previous part of this book, that it is impure and foul, and that which disobeys God, with evidence, so there is no need to repeat it in this place. Likewise, the meaning of immorality and His statement:
h
He has committed it to someone other than God
. All of that has been mentioned with sufficient evidence for whoever is guided to understand it, without repeating it or repeating it.

x: There is a difference in the reading of his statement, unless it is dead.

Some of the people of Medina, Kufa and Basra read it as: except that it is, with a yaa, “dead,” with a light yaa in the accusative case, on the basis that in “it is” is unknown, and dead is a verb for it, so it was in the accusative case because it is a verb of it is, and they mentioned it is, to remind the implied in it is.

Some of the readers of Mecca and Kufa read it as: illa an yakunu except that it is dead, with the ta’ of yā’ from yā’unu dead, with a light yā’ from yā’unu dead, and with its nasb lower case. The meaning of their nasb of yā’unu dead was the meaning of the first two, and they made it feminine to make it feminine, just as one says: innahu qayma’ jayyidati your slave girl, and innahu qayma’ jayyidati your slave girl, so the unknown is mentioned once and made feminine another time, to make the noun that comes after it feminine.

Some of the Medinans read it as: illa an yakunu except that it is dead, with the ta’ in yā’unu to be, and with a shaddah on the yā’ from yā’unu dead, and with its raf’ higher case, so they made yā’unu dead the noun of yā’unu dead, and they made yā’unu dead the feminine of yā’unu dead, and they made yā’unu suffice with the noun without the verb, because his saying: illa an yakunu ya’unu except that it is dead, is an exception, and the Arabs are satisfied with nouns instead of verbs in making an exception, so they say: the people stood Surat al-An’am 6:145 Say, "I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to one who would eat it unless it be a dead animal or blood poured forth or the flesh of swine - for indeed, it is impure - or an abomination dedicated to other than God.
h
But whoever is forced [by necessity]

, neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [it] - then indeed, your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful." up, illa an yā’u akhāka he is your brother, and illa an yā’u akhūka he is your brother, so they do not use d yā’un as a verb, and they make it independent of the noun, just as one says: the people stood up, illa an akhāka he is your brother, and illa an akhūka he is your brother, so the noun that comes after the letter of exception is not lacking a verb.

The correct reading of this in my opinion is: except that it is with the letter ya “dead,” with the letter ya softened and the word dead in the accusative case, because what is in it is is from the implied mention of the masculine, and it is: Say, I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to one who eats it unless it is a dead animal or blood poured forth. As for reading dead woman in the nominative case, since it is not wrong in Arabic, then the reading in this place is not correct. Because God says: or blood poured out, there is no disagreement among everyone in reading blood in the accusative case, and this is also the case in the copies of the Muslims’ Qur’ans, and it is in apposition to dead woman. So since that is the case, it is known that if dead woman were in the nominative case, then the blood and His saying: or transgression would be in the nominative case, but they are in the accusative case, so they are in apposition to it in the accusative case.
We have mentioned the difference of opinion among the people of interpretation in the interpretation of His statement:
h
But whoever is forced [by necessity]

, neither desiring [it] nor exceeding [its limits], and the correct statement regarding it, according to us, is what has preceded in this book of ours, in Surat al-Baqarah, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place, and that its meaning is: So whoever is forced to eat what God has forbidden, such as eating dead animals, spilled blood, or pork, or that which has been dedicated to other than God, not desiring to eat it out of enjoyment, not out of necessity due to a state of hunger, nor exceeding in eating it by exceeding what God has set and permitted him to eat, that is, he eats from it what will remove the fear for himself from dying by not eating it, he does not exceed that to more than that, so there is no blame upon him for eating what he has eaten of that, for God is Forgiving, in what he did of that, so He covered it up for him by not punishing him for it, and if He had willed, He would have punished him for it, Merciful, in permitting him to eat that when he needed it, and if He had willed, He would have forbidden it to him and prevented him from it.

evidence.text: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Al-Hajjaj bin Al-Munhal told us, he said, Hammad told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, on the authority of Al-Qasim bin Muhammad, on the authority of Aisha: that she did not see anything wrong with the meat of wild animals, and the redness and blood are wrong according to the quantity, and she recited this verse: Say, I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to one who would eat it.
Abu Jaafar said: There is a difference in the reading of his statement, unless it is dead.

Some of the people of Medina, Kufa and Basra read it as: except that it is, with a yaa, “dead,” with a light yaa in the accusative case, on the basis that in “it is” is unknown, and dead is a verb for it, so it was in the accusative case because it is a verb of it is, and they mentioned it is, to remind the implied in it is.
Some of the readers of Mecca and Kufa read it as: illa an yakunu except that it is dead, with the ta’ of yā’ from yā’unu dead, with a light yā’ from yā’unu dead, and with its nasb lower case.

Some of the Medinans read it as: illa an yakunu except that it is dead, with the ta’ in yā’unu to be, and with a shaddah on the yā’ from yā’unu dead, and with its raf’ higher case, so they made yā’unu dead the noun of yā’unu dead, and they made yā’unu dead the feminine of yā’unu dead, and they made yā’unu suffice with the noun without the verb, because his saying: illa an yakunu ya’unu except that it is dead, is an exception, and the Arabs are satisfied with nouns instead of verbs in making an exception, so they say: the people stood Surat al-An’am 6:145 Say, "I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to one who would eat it unless it be a dead animal or blood poured forth or the flesh of swine - for indeed, it is impure - or an abomination dedicated to other than God.

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct reading of this in my opinion is: except that it is with the letter ya “dead,” with the letter ya softened and the word dead in the accusative case, because what is in it is is from the implied mention of the masculine, and it is: Say, I do not find in what has been revealed to me anything forbidden to one who eats it unless it is a dead animal or blood poured forth.
As for reading dead woman in the nominative case, since it is not wrong in Arabic, then the reading in this place is not correct.

x: God Almighty says: And We have forbidden the Jews, everything with claws, which is from the beasts and birds unless it has split toes, such as camels, ostriches, geese, and ducks. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna and Ali bin Dawud told me, they said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah bin Saleh told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying:
h
And to those who are Jews
, We have forbidden every animal having claws, meaning the camel and the ostrich.

c: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, he said, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas:
m: h
And to those who are Jews
We have forbidden all animals having claws, he said: the camel, the ostrich, and similar animals.

c: Ibn Wakeeʿ told us, he said, Yahya ibn Adam told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of ʿAtaʿ, on the authority of Saʿid:
m: h
And to those who are Jews
We have forbidden all animals having claws, he said: it is that which does not have open fingers.

c: Ali bin Al-Hussein Al-Azdi told me, he said, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Ata bin Al-Saib, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair,
m: regarding his statement: And We have forbidden to those who are Jews every animal having claws, he said: Everything with separate digits, including the rooster.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said:
m: Everything with claws means the ostrich and the camel.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shibl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh,
m: similarly.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saʿid told us, on the authority of Qatada,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And to those who are Jews
We have forbidden every animal having claws, so it was said: the camel, the ostrich, and similar birds and whales.

c: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, he said, Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Everything with claws, he said: camels and ostriches, the claws of the camel’s hand and foot, and the ostrich is also like that. And what was also forbidden to them from the birds was ducks and the like, and everything that does not have split toes.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: As for everything with claws, it refers to camels and ostriches.

c: Al-Harith told me, he said, Abdul Aziz told us, he said, Sheikh told us, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding his statement:
h
And to those who are Jews

, We have forbidden every animal having claws, he said: The ostrich and the camel, split in two. I said: What is split in two? He said: Everything whose legs are not spread out, the Jews did not eat, and the camel and the ostrich. And the chickens and sparrows, the Jews eat, because they have spread out.

c: Al-Qasim told us, he said, Al-Hussein told us, he said, Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Everything having claws, he said: The ostrich and the camel, split in two. I said to Al-Qasim bin Abi Bazza, and he told me: What is split in two? He said: Everything that has not spread out from the hooves of animals. He said: And whatever has spread out, the Jews eat. He said: The legs of chickens and sparrows have spread out, so the Jews eat them. He said: The camel’s hoof, its hoof, and the ostrich’s hoof, and the hoof of the hyena, and the hoof of the hyena, are not separated. So the Jews do not eat camels, ostriches, or hyenas, nor anything whose hoof is not separated. Likewise, they do not eat a wild donkey. Ibn Zayd used to say about that as follows:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding His statement: And We have forbidden to those who are Jews every animal with claws, meaning camels.

x: The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the opinion that we mentioned on the authority of Ibn ʿAbbas and those who said something similar to his statement. Because God, the Most High, has informed us that He has forbidden the Jews everything with claws, so it is not permissible to exclude something that has died from the generality of this report except what the people of knowledge have agreed is excluded from it. If that is the case, and the ostrich and everything that is not from the beasts and birds that has claws other than open toes is included in the apparent meaning of the revelation, then it must be ruled that it is included in the report, since it did not come that some of that is not included in the verse, a report from God or from His Messenger, and the majority of the nation agreed that it is included in it.
The people of interpretation differed regarding the fats that God Almighty said that He forbade the Jews from cows and sheep.
Some of them said: They are the fats of sheep specifically.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada:
m: And of the cattle and the sheep
h
We have forbidden them their fat
, the fat. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say:
h
May God fight the Jews
, God forbade them the fat, then they ate its price.

x: Others said: Rather, it was any fat that was not mixed with bone or on bone.
Those who said that mentioned:

c: Al-Qasim told us, Al-Hussein told us, Hajjaj told me,
m: Ibn Jurayj said, regarding his statement:
h
We have forbidden them their fat
, he said: What was forbidden to them was the omentum, and all fat was like that except in a bone.

x: Others said: Rather, it is the fat of the omentum and kidneys.
Who said that?

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said,
m: Asbat, on the authority of Al-Suddi, regarding his statement:
h
We have forbidden them their fat
, he said: the omentum and the fat of the kidneys. The Jews used to say: Israel only forbade it, so we forbid it.

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
m: regarding his statement:
h
We have forbidden them their fat
, he said: He only forbade them the urinary tract and the kidneys. This is how it is in my book on the authority of Yunus, and I think that it is: the kidneys.

x: The correct statement in this regard is to say: God informed us that He had forbidden the Jews the fat of cows and sheep, except for what He had excluded from them, such as what their backs carried, or what was in their entrails, or what was mixed with a bone. So all fat, other than what God had excluded in His Book from cows and sheep, was forbidden to them. And similar to this statement, the report of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has been reported, and that is his saying:
h
May God fight the Jews
, the fat was forbidden to them, so they rendered it, then sold it and ate its price. As for his saying:
h
Except what their backs carry
, he means: except the fat of the sides and what is attached to the back, for it is not forbidden to them. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: h
Except what their backs carry
, meaning: what is attached to the back of the fat.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: As for what their backs carried, it means the buttocks.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Abu Saleh, he said:
m: The buttocks are what their backs carry.

x: Al-Hawaya is a plural, the singular of which is Hawiya, Hawiya, and Hawiya. It is what is contained in the stomach, so it gathers and becomes round. They are the daughters of milk, and they are the camels, and they are called the resting places, and they contain the intestines. The meaning of the statement is: And from the cows and the sheep,
h
We have forbidden them their fat

, except what their backs burn, or what the intestines carry. So Al-Hawaya is in the nominative case, in apposition to the back, and ma that comes after illa is in the accusative case as an exception from the fat. And the people of interpretation said the same as we said about that.
Who said that?

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Saleh told us, he said, Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas:
m: Or the Hawaya, which is the Ma’bar.

c: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said, Abu Asim told us, he said, Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid,
m: regarding the statement of God: or the depths, he said: the grave.

c: Al-Muthanna told me, he said, Abu Hudhayfah told us, he said, Shabl told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Al-Hawaya means the resting place and the den.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Shibl, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid:
m: Or the surroundings, he said: the spring.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahya bin Yaman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Sameed bin Jubair:
m: Or the camels, he said: the camels. Surat al-An’am 6:146 And We forbade to those who were Jews all animals having claws, and of the cattle and the sheep We forbade them their fat, except what adhered to their backs or the entrails or what was mixed with a bone.
h
That is how We recompensed them for their transgression
, and indeed, We are truthful.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Yahya bin Adam told us, on the authority of Sharik, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair:
m: Or the camels, he said: the camels.

c: Bishr told us, he said, Yazid told us, he said, Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada.
m: Or the Hawaya, he said: the Ma’bar.

c: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada:
m: Or the Hawaya, he said: the Ma’bar.

c: Ibn Wakee’ told us, he said, Abu Usamah and Al-Maharibi told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Al-Dahhak, he said:
m: Al-Mubar.

c: It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj,
m: who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd bin Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: or the insides, meaning the bellies other than the stomachs.

c: Muhammad bin Saad Qalʿ told me, my father told me, he said, my uncle told me, he said, my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas,
m: his saying: or the surroundings, it is the burial place.

c: Muhammad bin Al-Hussein told me, he said, Ahmad bin Al-Mufaddal told us, he said, Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi:
m: Or the camels, he said: the camels. Ibn Zayd said about this:

c: Yunus told me, he said, Ibn Wahb told us, he said, Ibn Zayd said
